item.title: TSA Agents Government Shutdown: The Airport Crisis Explained
item.description:
What happens when 480 airport security officers quit and thousands more stop showing up to work — all while millions of Americans are trying to fly? That’s not a hypothetical. It’s happening right now across U.S. airports as the Department of Homeland Security shutdown stretches past 40 days.

Key Takeaways

  • More than 480 TSA officers have quit since the DHS shutdown began on Feb. 14
  • TSA callout rates have more than doubled, from a normal 2% to over 6.1% nationwide
  • Roughly 60,000 TSA employees have gone nearly a month with reduced pay and received $0 paychecks
  • Wait times at some airports have exceeded three hours
  • President Trump ordered DHS to “immediately pay” TSA agents on March 26
  • TSA leadership warns of “long-standing” negative impacts even after funding is restored

TSA Agents Hit a “Breaking Point” as Paychecks Dry Up

The partial government shutdown, triggered when DHS funding lapsed on Feb. 13, has left roughly 60,000 TSA employees working without pay. As of this week, TSA staff prepared to miss a third consecutive paycheck, receiving $0 pay stubs — a gut punch for workers already under intense stress.

item.title: Erika Kirk Controversy: The Viral Smear, Legal Battles, and What's Really Happening
item.description:
A TikTok video racked up over 8 million views claiming Erika Kirk went on a $1,000 shopping spree hours after her husband Charlie Kirk was assassinated. The correction from an eyewitness staffer? Buried in replies most of those 8 million people will never see.

Key Takeaways

  • A viral TikTok accused Erika Kirk of spending $1,000 at Alo Yoga the morning after Charlie Kirk’s death — a TPUSA staffer says she made the purchase, not Erika
  • Erika Kirk’s legal team has now sent three cease-and-desist letters over defamation claims
  • Candace Owens, Joe Rogan, and others have publicly questioned Kirk, intensifying conservative infighting
  • Alo Yoga may face legal consequences for an employee allegedly leaking Kirk’s private purchase history

Erika Kirk and the Alo Yoga Smear That Went Viral

The claim spread fast. A TikTok creator with nearly 900,000 followers posted a video alleging that someone who worked at Alo Yoga had sent him a receipt showing Erika Kirk spent over $1,000 at the store less than 24 hours after Charlie Kirk was assassinated at Utah Valley University. “That is not how shock works,” the creator said. “That is not how grief works for a normal person.”

item.title: Arctic Frost: The FBI Investigation Shaking Washington in 2026
item.description:
Have you ever heard of a single code name that could define an entire political era? Arctic Frost — the FBI investigation into efforts to overturn the 2020 presidential election — has exploded back into the national spotlight, drawing comparisons to Watergate and fueling a constitutional crisis over political retaliation within federal law enforcement.

Key Takeaways

  • “Arctic Frost” was an FBI probe opened in April 2022 investigating the alleged false electors scheme after the 2020 election.
  • Two fired FBI agents have sued Director Kash Patel and Attorney General Pam Bondi, alleging their terminations were politically motivated.
  • Senate hearings labeled the controversy “A Modern Watergate,” with heated testimony on March 24, 2026.
  • The investigation involved 197 subpoenas to 34 individuals and 163 businesses, covering more than 400 Republican figures and entities.

What Is Operation Arctic Frost?

Arctic Frost was the code name assigned to a federal investigation launched in April 2022. Its original purpose was to examine whether President Donald Trump committed wrongdoing in the alleged “false electors scheme” following the 2020 presidential election.

item.title: Lindsey Graham Under Fire: Iran War Rhetoric Sparks GOP Civil War and Reelection Crisis
item.description:
Has a single weekend ever done more damage to a sitting senator’s standing within his own party? Lindsey Graham’s call for the United States to seize Iran’s Kharg Island has ignited a firestorm — not from Democrats, but from fellow Republicans who say the South Carolina senator is treating American troops like “expendable cattle.”

Key Takeaways

  • Graham urged President Trump to “take Kharg Island” and let Iran’s regime “die on a vine,” comparing the operation to Iwo Jima.
  • Multiple MAGA-aligned Republicans — including Marjorie Taylor Greene and Nancy Mace — publicly denounced his rhetoric.
  • Graham’s approval rating in South Carolina sits at just 34 percent, making his 2026 reelection bid one of the most vulnerable in the Senate.
  • Trump has endorsed Graham and dispatched former campaign manager Chris LaCivita to advise his campaign.

Lindsey Graham’s Kharg Island Push Draws Bipartisan Outrage

Over the weekend, Senator Graham appeared on Fox News and made a bold pitch: he urged President Donald Trump to order a military strike on Kharg Island, a critical hub for Iran’s oil exports.

item.title: Kyrsten Sinema's Mounting Legal and Political Troubles: Lawsuits, Campaign Finance Questions, and a New Media Role
item.description:
Former U.S. Senator Kyrsten Sinema, once a trailblazing figure in Arizona politics, is now at the center of a rapidly expanding web of legal battles, financial accusations, and personal scandals. In the span of just a few months, Sinema has gone from political maverick to tabloid fixture, facing an alienation of affection lawsuit, campaign finance allegations totaling $700,000, and the very public fallout of an admitted affair.

As of March 13, 2026, she is fighting to have the lawsuit dismissed while simultaneously launching a new career as a columnist for a conservative Washington news outlet. The convergence of these stories has made Sinema one of the most talked-about former lawmakers in the country.
